usageNotes: Use this to stop a running or queued task on a PDM node by its UPID. Users can stop their own tasks without elevated privileges; stopping another user's task requires Sys.Modify on /system/tasks. The UPID must match a task that is still active — sending a DELETE against an already-finished task is a no-op (returns null without error).

examples.summary: Stop a running vzdump backup task on node pdm-node1

destructiveReason: Terminates the targeted running task, which may leave in-progress operations (e.g., backups, migrations, or replication syncs) in an incomplete or inconsistent state.
tips: The UPID pattern is strict — obtain it from list_nodes_node_tasks rather than constructing it manually.
A DELETE on a task that has already completed returns null with no error; check task status first if you need to confirm it was actually running.
Stopping a backup or replication task mid-run may leave partial snapshots or dirty state on the target datastore that requires manual cleanup.
